title: config
description: What every field of the design is called and how it is drawn, from config: the definitions in use after every layer, where each entry came from, and what the design cannot offer, so a reader draws the design without knowing the layers.

apiVersion.description: Always elderlygate/designer/app/v1: the form of e-designer's answers. An app's answers keep the family app (apiversion/v1/forms.yaml), apart from the files they describe.

kind.description: Always Config, the kind of this answer, so a reader knows which schema its data meets.

ran.description: Where the answer came from; this contract fixes the app and the contract version, so an answer from anything else fails here.

app.description: Always designer, e-designer's product ID, since only e-designer gives this answer.

contract.description: Always v1, the contract version this schema belongs to.

data.description: The definitions the design reads, and their sources.

sections.description: One row per definitions section asked for, saying where each entry came from, so a reader can tell the design's own entries from the built-in ones.

design.description: The design's definitions file, by its path in the design, where an entry marked design comes from, so a reader can open it; relative, so an answer over HTTP gives no folder of the serving machine away. Absent when no design was read.

entries.description: Every entry of the section by name, and where the one in use came from.

additionalProperties.description: Where the value in use came from: built-in, e-designer's own, or design, the design's definitions.yml.

settings.description: The design's settings in use and where each came from; absent when one section was asked for.

design.description: The design's definitions file, by its path in the design, where a setting marked design comes from, so a reader can open it; relative, so an answer over HTTP gives no folder of the serving machine away. Absent when no design was read.

entries.description: Every setting by name, and where the one in use came from.

additionalProperties.description: Where the value in use came from: built-in, e-designer's own, or design, the design's definitions.yml.

exportTo.description: Where the register export writes; absent means no export.

register.description: The headings, markers and columns of the exported register, one table per kind; absent means the built-in ones.

items.description: One kind's table in the register.

heading.description: The heading the table is written under, so the export finds where it goes.

marker.description: The marker that finds the table in the document, so the export replaces only its own table.

label.description: The column's heading, as people read it in the register.

from.description: The field the column is read from, so the export knows what to write in it.

strip.description: Text taken off the value before it is written; absent takes nothing off.

whereDocument.description: Which document a component's where[] points into; absent means the export target's own file name.

diagrams.description: The headings component diagrams are read under; absent means the built-in ones.

items.description: One heading, under which a diagram is read.

definitions.description: The definitions in use after every layer: classes, properties, sections, presentations, schemas, features and vocabulary. Their entries are the design's own words, written by its user, so they stay open (CT-RULE-4); config's sections say where each came from.

problems.description: Every definition e-designer could not take, so a reader shows why something is not drawn as written. The board section's problems are not here: DesignContents.board.problems holds them, one place for each fact.

moved.description: Entries a newer e-designer moved to another place, one sentence each, so a reader can tell the user to move them in the file.

items.description: One moved entry, in words for people.

releaseLanes.description: The ways a view may lay its blocks out by release, so a reader offers e-designer's list rather than keeping its own.

items.description: One way, such as rows or columns.

purposes.description: The purposes a design may count as, read even when the design's own list is broken, so a reader offers the right words.

value.description: The word, as design.yml writes it.

note.description: What the purpose means, for people; absent when the list says nothing.

default.description: The purpose of a design whose design.yml states none.

notSet.description: How a design that states no purpose is named, such as reference (not set), so a reader uses e-designer's words.

apiVersion.description: The form a new design file is written in, so a reader that writes one takes e-designer's and keeps no copy.

origins.description: Every kind and where it comes from, so a reader can tell a kind the project adds from a built-in kind it amends.

additionalProperties.description: built-in: e-designer's own; project: the design declares it; extended: a built-in kind the design's definitions.yml amends.

unavailable.description: Every feature the design cannot offer, because it does not declare a kind the feature requires, and how to show it; a feature not listed is on offer. e-designer judges it, so a reader only draws the answer.

additionalProperties.description: How the feature is shown while the design cannot offer it.

oneOf.description: Not shown at all, as the feature asks with whenUndefined: invisible.
Shown greyed out with why, the default.

reason.description: Why the feature is not on offer, the feature's own words or the kinds it needs, for people.
